Overview: AQUARIUM GAME — COMBINED ECONOMY & PROGRESSION MODEL v3
The economy now uses target-rate payouts. Fish output is based on role, unlock level, schedule factor, and rarity utility budget — not Buy Price × rarity × growth-time multipliers.

Every fish has a purpose: schedule purpose (active/session/idle), economic purpose (coin, XP, balanced, payout, convenience), and collection/aquarium purpose (mastery, prestige, social, theme). See Coin Fish AA:AB.
Premium and Limited Edition fish are capped. Pearls buy visual exclusivity, convenience, XP/action, and collection progress, not a dominant coin printer.
Egg → Junior (25%) → Young (55%) → Mature (80%) → Adult (100%). Stage Time is one age level; Adult = 4 × Stage Time.
Stage-specific XP now exists for Junior, Young, Mature, and Adult selling. Buy XP is 8% of the full-cycle XP budget, so selling stage choices are meaningful.
Sickness grace is proportional: MAX(minimum grace, feed window × 25%), capped at 24h. This fixes the old problem where 5-minute fish effectively had absurdly generous protection.
XP Curve smooths the L10/L11 and L30/L31 transitions while retaining a months-long L70 aspiration for a core player.
Tank costs were repriced as meaningful coin sinks. Fish purchases are working capital; tanks, capacity, maintenance, food, decor and event crafting remove long-term surplus.
Quest rewards are no longer static. Quest Scaling sets daily XP to roughly 10% of next-level XP and weekly XP to roughly 45%.
Start from Dashboard and Balance Review. Edit yellow input cells and blue balancing tables on Inputs; fish sheets will reprice through formulas.
To add a post-launch fish, copy it from Roadmap into Coin Fish or Premium Fish and assign a role before tuning art/value details.
